text:
Its a bakery at 3:17 AM, the mixer is just humming, really loud, vibration goes through my boots. Its dark and flour dust is all over the air, catching the fluorescent light, looks like snow hanging there. The sourdough loaves are on wooden boards, still pale soft, not done with the final bake. I wipe my hands on the apron. Its stiff, dried dough and sweat. I move to the counter to check the lock. Its not needed really, just paranoid, a ritual.
There it was. The History of Salt, hardback, blue spine cracked near the hinge. Every Thursday for six weeks its been there, put exactly on the glass display case, next to the unsold cinnamon rolls. No library stamp, and we are not a branch of the municipal system, so where does it come from. I picked it up, felt cold. I opened it and expected blank pages or some forgotten bookmark. Instead a square of lined notebook paper folded up slipped out, hit the counter, soft tap. I unfolded it. The handwriting was jagged, pressed hard into the fiber. It said, You knead with your left hand dominant, stop favoring the right, it ruins the tension. I just stared at it. The mixer ticked over to the next cycle. I look at my hands, red knuckled, dusted white. I closed the book. I put it back on the glass, aligned the spine perfectly with the edge. Then I turn off the overhead light above the display. Book is now in shadow.
